<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/../src/Accessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/JsonAccessor.php';

use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\EnvAccessor;
use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\JsonAccessor;

$failures = 0;
function check(string $name, bool $ok): void
{
    global $failures;
    echo ($ok ? "ok   " : "FAIL ") . $name . "\n";
    if (!$ok) {
        $failures++;
    }
}

$env = new EnvAccessor("HOST=localhost\nPORT=3000\n");
check('reads KEY=value lines', $env->get('HOST') === 'localhost' && $env->get('PORT') === '3000');

$env = new EnvAccessor("# a comment\n\nKEY=value\n");
check('skips blank lines and comments', $env->all() === ['KEY' => 'value']);

$env = new EnvAccessor("A=\"one two\"\nB='three'\n");
check('strips one pair of matching quotes', $env->get('A') === 'one two' && $env->get('B') === 'three');

$env = new EnvAccessor('KEY=value');
check('answers the fallback for a key that is not there', $env->get('MISSING', 'none') === 'none' && $env->has('KEY') && !$env->has('MISSING'));

$json = new JsonAccessor('{"name":"x","count":3}');
check('json keeps the string values of an object', $json->all() === ['name' => 'x']);

exit($failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

content.text: Both suites pass. The `export` prefix rules are a choice someone could question later, so I'm recording them.

input.title: EnvAccessor strips a leading `export` only when a space or tab follows it, in both packages
input.rationale: `export KEY=value` lines read as KEY=value, as if the prefix were absent. The prefix is `export` followed by one or more spaces or tabs (`/^export[ \t]+/`), removed after the blank/comment check and the trim, so `# export X=1` stays a comment, and `export=1` and `exported=2` remain ordinary keys. A bare `export FLAG` has no `=` and is skipped like any other line without one. The same regex and order are used in packages/js and packages/php, as ADR-1 requires, with equivalent tests in both. `[ \t]` is chosen over `\s` because JS `\s` matches Unicode whitespace while PHP's non-/u `\s` matches only ASCII, which would make the two packages disagree on exotic whitespace.
input.alternatives: `/^export\s+/`: rejected, `\s` differs between JS (Unicode) and PHP (ASCII), a parity gap. Strip any `export` token even without whitespace (`startsWith('export')`): rejected, it would turn the legitimate keys `export` and `exported` into wrong keys. Change only the JS package or only PHP: rejected by ADR-1, the gap is the defect. Also accept `export` with quoting or `declare -x`: not asked for, left out to keep the parser plain.

`EnvAccessor` now reads `export KEY=value` as `KEY=value`, in both the JS and PHP packages. I haven't committed anything. Both test suites pass: 9 of 9 in JS, and every check in `php packages/php/tests/run.php`.

The repo's accepted ADR-1 says a behavior change in one package is made in the other in the same pull request. So I changed both `EnvAccessor`s the same way: after the blank-line and comment check, a leading `export` followed by spaces or tabs is stripped.

- **Prefix handling:** `# export X=1` is still a comment. `export=1` and `exported=2` stay ordinary keys, and a bare `export FLAG` is skipped because it has no `=`. Indented lines and `\r\n` endings work.
- **Why not `\s`:** the pattern is `/^export[ \t]+/` rather than `/^export\s+/`. In JS `\s` also matches Unicode whitespace, but PHP's version matches only ASCII, so the two packages would have disagreed.
- **New tests:** three in each package, in `packages/js/tests/env-accessor.test.ts` and `packages/php/tests/run.php`. One covers the basic prefix, quoting and the key name. One covers indentation and `\r\n`. One covers what only looks like the prefix.
- **Record:** I recorded this as ADR-2. It is still `proposed`, so a person or agent needs to accept it.
